title: Fluids, Density and Buoyancy
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Fluids, Density and Buoyancy Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the properties of fluids, including viscosity and density; calculate density; explain buoyancy and why objects float or sink, using the particle theory. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Fluids)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 science worksheets on fluids, viscosity, density calculations, floating and sinking, and buoyancy. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Objects float in fluids that are denser than they are; viscosity is resistance to flow.
body_html:
How to think about it

A fluid is anything that flows: liquids and gases.

  • Viscosity is a fluid's resistance to flow (honey is viscous); warming usually lowers viscosity.
  • Density = mass ÷ volume. Water is 1 g/cm³ (1 g/mL).
  • An object floats if it is less dense than the fluid. Buoyant force pushes up.
Example

A block has a mass of 60 g and a volume of 100 cm³. Will it float in water?

60 ÷ 100 = 0.6 g/cm³

0.6 < 1

Answer: yes, it floats

Example

Oil and water are poured in a glass. Which is on top?

oil is less dense

Answer: oil

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up viscosity and density.
  • Thinking heavy objects always sink (density matters, not weight).
  • Dividing volume by mass instead of mass by volume.

faq.q: What is the difference between viscosity and density?
faq.a: Viscosity is how easily a fluid flows. Density is how much mass is packed into a volume.

faq.q: Why does a steel ship float?
faq.a: Its hollow shape holds lots of air, so the ship's overall density is less than water.
Divide the mass by the volume. For example, 50 g ÷ 25 cm³ = 2 g/cm³.

c: It changes from a gas to a liquid.
It changes from a solid to a gas.
It changes from a solid to a liquid.

items.q: A steel ship floats, but a steel bolt sinks. Why?
c: The ship's hollow shape displaces a lot of water, so its overall density is less than water.
Steel floats when it is cold.
items.e: Shape changes overall density.

items.q: What is a fluid?
c: a substance that can flow, like a liquid or a gas
items.e: Air and water are both fluids.

items.q: What is buoyancy?
c: the upward force a fluid puts on an object
items.e: It is also called the buoyant force.

items.q: What is viscosity?
items.e: Honey has a high viscosity.

items.q: How does a submarine dive?
c: It pumps out all the air and floats.
It lets water into its tanks to become denser than the water around it.
items.e: To rise, it pushes the water out with air.

items.q: What did Archimedes discover?
c: The buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid an object pushes aside.
items.e: This is Archimedes' principle.

items.q: Which state of matter can easily be squashed (compressed)?
items.e: Use the particle model: arrangement, movement and forces.

items.e: Changes of state are physical changes.

items.q: What happens to a substance when it is boiling?

items.q: Which state of matter cannot be poured and keeps its shape?

items.q: Why does ice float on water?
c: Water pushes ice up because it is colder.
Ice is less dense than liquid water.
items.e: This keeps lakes from freezing solid.

items.q: Why are oil spills especially harmful to sea birds?
c: Oil makes birds heavier than air only.
Oil coats feathers so they lose buoyancy and warmth.
items.e: Spills damage ecosystems.

items.q: What is the name for a change from a solid to a gas?
items.e: Melting, freezing, boiling, condensing and sublimating.

items.q: Which fluid has the highest viscosity?

items.q: Why is it easier to float in the Dead Sea than in Lake Ontario?
c: Salty water is denser, so it gives more buoyant force.
items.e: Denser fluids push up harder.

items.q: What is density?
c: the mass of a substance in a certain volume
items.e: Density = mass ÷ volume.

items.q: Which state of matter has the strongest forces between its particles?

items.q: Why does motor oil come in different viscosities for winter and summer?

Oil does not change with temperature.
items.e: Temperature affects viscosity.
